name: Legislative/Lobby Committee Liaison Meeting Agenda
minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Legislative / Lobby Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Friday, March 8, 2024
  11:00 AM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  March 8, 2024 / 11:00 AM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Julian Gold, Councilmember John Mirisch, Deputy City Manager
  Keith Sterling, Municipal Affairs Program Manager Cynthia Owens

  A. Oral Communications:

  None

  B. Direction:
  1. 2024 Legislative Platform
  i. The city is advocating to move RHNA back to a planning tool rather than a
  punitive punishment for cities that fail to reach their targets. A duplicated
  version of this statement is also being deleted from the platform.
  ii. Staff decided to focus on removing duplicated or similar statements from
  the Legislative Platform that are already covered by existing statements.
  iii. Staff also removed any references to COVID-19 for fiscal and
  administrative initiatives, and instead replaced it with “natural or man-made
  disasters”.
  iv. Councilmember Mirisch indicated his preference for staff to add a part to
  the Legislative Platform stating the city’s support for Israel.
  v. Mayor Gold indicated his support for adding a section focusing on
  protecting citizens from utilities unilaterally changing prices or terms of
  access. This also would include protecting citizens from utility failures.
  However, the liaisons are opposed to redistributive measures and would
  prefer private utilities also be held to a similar standard as Prop 218.
  vi. Mayor Gold wishes to add a section about protecting kids from the dangers
  of social media and AI.
  2. S.2632 - Visa Processing Improvement Act
  i. Senate bill that would address processing times for tourist and temporary
  work visas.
  ii. Comments by Julie Wagner
  1. A large percentage of tourism to Beverly Hills comes from foreign
  countries.
  2. International tourism has still not recovered to pre-pandemic levels,
  despite projections that it would be fully recovered by 2025.
 Highlights for March 8, 2024
Legislative / Lobby Committee

  iii. Councilmember Mirsch had concerns about this supporting Iran and Qatar.
  The committee promised to get back to him about the specifics but believe
  that Iran would not be included.
  iv. Mayor Gold is in support of the legislation.
  3. H.R.6859 - Gabrielino/Tongva Nation Recognition Act of 2023
  i. Cut for time.
  4. Assembly Bill 1999 (Irwin) - Electricity; fixed charges
  i. Cut for time.
  5. Assembly Bill 2584 (Lee) - Single-family residential real property: corporate entity:
  ownership
  i. Cut for time.
  6. Senate Bill 1212 (Skinner) - Investment entities: purchasing, acquiring, or leasing
  interests in housing
  i. Cut for time.
  7. Senate Bill 915 (Cortese - Local government: autonomous vehicles
  i. Cut for time.
  8. Ballot Initiative (22-0008) - Expands Local Governments’ Authority to Enact Rent
  Control on Residential Property.
  i. Cut for time.
  9. Assembly Bill 2230 (Bennett) - Residential Housing Unfair Practices Act of 2023
  i. Cut for time.
  10. Legislative Updates
  i. The committee discussed President Biden’s state of the Union Speech and
  how Democrats see it as a strong point for Biden.
  ii. The rebuttal was not well received by both Democrats and Republicans.
  iii. California is projected to run a large deficit in FY 2024-25, with the most
  recent report projecting a deficit of $73 billion. In response to this
  Sacramento is looking for a number of ways to reduce spending including
  budget cuts.
  11. Future Agenda Items Discussion
  i. None

  C. Adjournment:
  Date / Time: March 8, 2024 / 12:04 PM
